blocks.text: Release overview

iOS 15.0 was publicly released on September 20, 2021. iOS 15.0 was the annual platform release, combining major communication and attention-management changes with redesigns across Maps, Safari, Wallet, Weather, and other built-in apps.
FaceTime links, Focus, notification summaries, Live Text, and broader on-device intelligence formed the core public feature set. Availability varied by device, language, and region.
Release overview
iOS 15.1 was publicly released on October 25, 2021. iOS 15.1 delivered the delayed SharePlay experience and expanded camera, health-record, translation, and Home capabilities.
The release made shared playback available in FaceTime, added ProRes capture on supported iPhone 13 Pro models, and let Wallet store verifiable COVID-19 vaccination cards.
Release overview
iOS 15.2 was publicly released on December 13, 2021. iOS 15.2 expanded privacy, family safety, account legacy, music, mail, and device-location capabilities.
App Privacy Report and Communication Safety were the most visible policy-oriented additions, accompanied by Digital Legacy, the Apple Music Voice Plan, and refinements to Mail and Find My.
Release overview
iOS 15.2.1 was publicly released on January 12, 2022. iOS 15.2.1 was a focused maintenance release for Messages, third-party CarPlay apps, and a disclosed HomeKit denial-of-service issue.
Apple documented two user-facing fixes and one CVE-tracked HomeKit correction; this batch does not infer additional changes.
Release overview
iOS 15.3 was publicly released on January 26, 2022. iOS 15.3 was a maintenance and security release rather than a feature-focused update.
Apple’s consumer note remains general, so this batch preserves a coarse maintenance entry and relies on the advisory for disclosed security content.
Release overview
iOS 15.3.1 was publicly released on February 10, 2022. iOS 15.3.1 paired a Braille-display responsiveness fix with a WebKit security correction.
Apple said the WebKit issue might have been actively exploited, making the security change the defining part of this small release.
Release overview
iOS 15.4 was publicly released on March 14, 2022. iOS 15.4 was a substantial point release centered on masked authentication, communication features, health records, Siri, and new emoji.
Face ID with a mask on supported iPhone 12 and later models was the headline addition, alongside expanded SharePlay entry points and EU Digital COVID Certificate support.
Release overview
iOS 15.4.1 was publicly released on March 31, 2022. iOS 15.4.1 was a corrective update for battery drain and accessibility-device behavior, with an urgent media-decoder security fix.
The release addressed battery depletion after iOS 15.4, Braille-device responsiveness, and Made for iPhone hearing-device connectivity.
Release overview
iOS 15.5 was publicly released on May 16, 2022. iOS 15.5 refined Apple Cash and Podcasts while correcting Home automation and iPhone SE reliability issues.
The point release was incremental: Wallet gained direct send and request controls, and Podcasts gained storage-management settings.
Release overview
iOS 15.6 was publicly released on July 20, 2022. iOS 15.6 added live-sports playback controls in the TV app and bundled several storage, accessibility, and Safari fixes.
Apple’s notes identify a small set of user-facing corrections rather than a broad feature release.
Release overview
iOS 15.6.1 was publicly released on August 17, 2022. iOS 15.6.1 was a security-focused release addressing kernel and WebKit vulnerabilities.
Apple said both disclosed issues may have been actively exploited; no separate consumer feature delta was documented.
Release overview
iOS 15.7 was publicly released on September 12, 2022. iOS 15.7 continued the iOS 15 line as a security-focused maintenance release.
Apple’s consumer note identifies important security updates and does not describe a new feature set.
Release overview

iPadOS 15.0 was publicly released on September 20, 2021. iPadOS 15.0 was the annual platform release, emphasizing multitasking discoverability, flexible Home Screen organization, faster note capture, and the communication and attention features shared with iOS 15.
A new multitasking menu, App Shelf, Home Screen widgets, App Library, Quick Note, Focus, and Live Text reshaped everyday iPad workflows.
Release overview
iPadOS 15.1 was publicly released on October 25, 2021. iPadOS 15.1 delivered SharePlay and enabled Live Text in the Camera app while expanding translation, Home, and Shortcuts support.
The release completed a prominent delayed FaceTime feature and broadened camera-based text recognition on supported iPads.
Release overview
iPadOS 15.2 was publicly released on December 13, 2021. iPadOS 15.2 expanded privacy reporting, family safety, account legacy, media, note-taking, and mail capabilities.
App Privacy Report, Communication Safety, and Digital Legacy arrived alongside the Apple Music Voice Plan and several iPad-specific workflow refinements.
Release overview
iPadOS 15.3 was publicly released on January 26, 2022. iPadOS 15.3 was a maintenance and security release rather than a feature-focused update.
Apple’s consumer note remains general, so this batch does not invent a detailed user-facing change list.
Release overview
iPadOS 15.4 was publicly released on March 14, 2022. iPadOS 15.4 introduced Universal Control and expanded communication, Siri, keyboard, camera, and volume-control behavior.
Universal Control was the defining iPad feature, allowing a nearby Mac’s keyboard, mouse, or trackpad to work across supported Macs and iPads.
Release overview
iPadOS 15.5 was publicly released on May 16, 2022. iPadOS 15.5 was an incremental maintenance release centered on Podcasts storage management and security fixes.
Apple documented one consumer-facing Podcasts setting and a broader set of security corrections.
Release overview
iPadOS 15.6 was publicly released on July 20, 2022. iPadOS 15.6 added live-sports playback controls and corrected storage, accessibility, Safari, and iPad mini connectivity issues.
The release combined a small TV app enhancement with targeted maintenance fixes, including USB-C accessory detection on iPad mini (6th generation).
Release overview
iPadOS 15.7 was publicly released on September 12, 2022. iPadOS 15.7 continued the iPadOS 15 line as a security-focused maintenance release.
Apple’s consumer note identifies important security updates and does not describe a new feature set.

events.summary: iOS 15.0 reached the public release channel on September 20, 2021. iOS 15.0 was the annual platform release, combining major communication and attention-management changes with redesigns across Maps, Safari, Wallet, Weather, and other built-in apps. This article records the public appearance only and does not attribute cumulative notes to an earlier beta.

blocks.text: Public release
Apple’s dated release record places iOS 15.0 on September 20, 2021. This article records that public appearance only and does not assign the cumulative version notes to any preceding beta.
What changed
FaceTime links, Focus, notification summaries, Live Text, and broader on-device intelligence formed the core public feature set. Availability varied by device, language, and region.

changes.title: FaceTime links and expanded calls
changes.canonicalSummary: FaceTime gained shareable call links, spatial-audio placement, voice isolation, Wide Spectrum, grid view, and Portrait mode.
changes.summary: The public release expanded FaceTime calling and allowed people on Android or Windows to join supported calls in a browser.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Focus and notification summary
changes.canonicalSummary: Focus filters notifications by context, while scheduled summaries collect lower-priority notifications for later delivery.
changes.summary: iOS 15 introduced Focus profiles, status sharing, redesigned notifications, and scheduled delivery summaries.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Maps redesign and Live Text
changes.canonicalSummary: Maps gained richer navigation detail, while Live Text recognizes actionable text in photos and supported camera views.
changes.summary: The release paired expanded Maps detail and transit tools with system recognition of text in images.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.

changes.title: Safari and Shared with You
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari adopted a redesigned tab experience, and Shared with You surfaced content received in Messages inside supported apps.
changes.summary: Safari added Tab Groups and extensions, while supported Apple apps collected shared links, photos, music, and other content.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched first-party Apple documentation to the audited public-release version and date.
